But, as stated.. I'm a surgeon in a senior position with 11 years of experience. I'm not exclusively bariatric, originally specialized as a colorectal surgeon but we all do lots of other stuff as well, the specialities are not as rigid as in the UK/US. So, I've been doing bariatric surgeries since about 2,5 y, and have my fair share of morbidly obese "normal" patients as well, ones with cancer or appendicitis and stuff like that.

We do Roux - Y Bypasses, if you want to look it up, except for people over 250 - 260 kg (kg mind you, not pounds) where we sometimes start off with a sleeve resection especially if they're older or very ill and come back for Roux- Y later, when they have lost 10% excess body weight. Oh yes, all those percentages of weight loss post-surgery are given as % of excess body weight, not total weight so Mister 280 kg loses 18-20kg and we're happy. Really. Roux-Y post surgery tend to do rather well, 20-40% weight loss, no diabetes any more. Goes overnight. Everything else is up to them. It is difficult to cheat a Roux-Y, but they find ways. Down-side is that they are malnourished and have a vitamin deficiency for the rest of their lives.

HEAS is absolutely frustrating for me. It is not very prevalent in my country but slowly creeping up in the corners. But I'm used to hearing so many excuses and bullshit from the alcoholics, the drug addicts, the smokers, the people who believe they won't get cancer if they "live healthy" the anti-vaxxers etc. it's exactly the same sentences you hear from the fats.
